request.spec:
When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the
number is not given to anyone else). Show the number on the claim. Every audit line about a
claim that has a number gains number=<number> at its end (so CLAIM_OPENED and CLAIM_SETTLED
carry it; a CLAIM_VOIDED line carries the number the claim had).

When a claim is opened it receives the next number on the sheet: 1 for the first claim ever
opened on the sheet, then 2, and so on, with no gaps and never reused, even when two users open
claims at the same moment. A draft has no number, and voiding a claim clears its number (the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now get a number when they're opened, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the one where two users open claims at the same moment.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V7__claim_number.sql`, adds a `number_on_sheet` column to `claim`. It also adds a `claim_number` table that holds the last number given out on each sheet.
- **Server:** opening a claim increments that sheet's counter and gives the result to the claim, as part of the request's existing database transaction (`Claims.java`, `ApplyClaimStatus.java`).
  - The counter row stays locked until the transaction commits, so two claims opened at once get different numbers.
  - If two users open the very first claim on a sheet at the same moment, the one that loses the race takes the next number instead.
  - An open that's refused is turned down before any number is taken, and a failure after that rolls the counter back, so there are no gaps.
- **Voiding:** clears the claim's number, and the number is never handed out again because the counter only goes up.
- **Audit:** `CLAIM_OPENED`, `CLAIM_SETTLED` and `CLAIM_VOIDED` lines end with `number=<n>` when the claim has a number. Voiding a draft writes no number, since a draft never had one.
- **Front end:** each claim row shows `#<n>`, with the number in a `claim-number` element that is empty for drafts and voided claims (`claims.slot.tsx`, `claims.ts`).
